_comment: Paste this JSON into the detection_criteria field when creating the AttackVector for the phishing stage via Django admin or API.
indicator_descriptions: Spoofed domain: 'linkedln.com' (note the 'n' replacing 'i') instead of 'linkedin.com'
Urgency manipulation: '48-hour deadline' and URGENT badge pressure tactics (T1566)
Suspicious file extension: 'JobOffer_TechCorp.pdf.exe' — double extension malware delivery (T1204)
Mismatched sender domain: sarah.reynolds@techcorp-global.net does not match 'TechCorp Global'
Unrealistic salary promise: $180,000–$220,000 with no interview process
success_message: Correct — you identified this as a phishing attempt. You spotted the attack before engaging with the attacker.
miss_explanation: This was a phishing message. The link used a lookalike domain (linkedln.com vs linkedin.com), the attachment had a double extension (.pdf.exe) which is a common malware delivery technique, and the message used urgency manipulation to pressure you into acting quickly.
best_practice: Always verify the sender's domain, hover over links to inspect the actual URL before clicking, and never download attachments from unsolicited recruiters without verifying their identity through an official channel.
mitre_description: Phishing — adversaries send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems
